title: Wounds from Others
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Wounds from others are harms caused by the sins, failures, neglect, abuse, betrayal, or cruelty of people. Scripture teaches that God sees these wounds and calls His people toward truth, wisdom, healing, justice, forgiveness, and hope in Christ.
summary: Wounds from others are harms caused by the sins, failures, neglect, abuse, betrayal, or cruelty of people. Scripture teaches that God sees these wounds and calls His people toward truth, wisdom, healing, justice, forgiveness, and hope in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ was betrayed, rejected, falsely accused, and wounded by sinners. He understands wounds from others and brings mercy, justice, and restoration to those who suffer.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Not all suffering is caused by a person’s own sin. Many wounds come from what others have done. Scripture gives language for betrayal, oppression, slander, abandonment, violence, and grief.

God sees harm. He does not ask the wounded to pretend evil was good or insignificant. He is a righteous Judge and a compassionate refuge for the brokenhearted.

Healing from wounds requires truth and wisdom. Some wounds call for forgiveness, boundaries, justice, lament, counsel, and time. Restoration should never be forced in a way that ignores repentance or safety.

Christ is near to the wounded because He Himself was rejected and harmed. He entrusted Himself to the Father who judges justly, and He helps His people walk in truth without being destroyed by vengeance.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People wounded by others often carry confusion, shame, anger, fear, and mistrust. They may wonder whether God cares about what happened. This doctrine says clearly that He sees and cares.

It also protects against spiritual simplifications that rush wounded people into silence. Biblical care names harm truthfully while pointing to Christ’s healing and justice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name wounds honestly before God. Seek wise help, refuse revenge, pursue safety where needed, and entrust justice to the Lord. Let Christ meet you in pain and teach you how to walk toward healing without denying truth.
